clue.text: Fishing smack? What nonsense!

definitions.meaning: read as a fish's blow: a ..., a smack delivered by a fish
an exclamation dismissing something as rubbish or drivel

explanation.walkthrough: A fishing smack is really a kind of boat; here it is taken as a smack (a wallop) belonging to a fish, the cod.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for rubbish talk, used as an exclamation of disbelief.

clue.text: If tailless the end would become a fish

definitions.text: If tailless the end would become a fish

parts.words: If tailless the end would become a fish
parts.note: a word meaning the end, a musical finale, which with its last letter docked turns into the name of a common food fish

explanation.walkthrough: The musical term for a closing passage loses its final A and leaves a sea fish, so the clue describes the word by what happens when it is cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the closing section of a piece is this term, so it is literally the finish.

clue.text: An. Indian city see vague outline

indicators.note: the city sits inside the word for vague, so 'in' here places one piece within the other

parts.note: dim means faint or vague
Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal

explanation.surface: A hazy, faint sketch of an Indian city's skyline.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawing that shows the shape or plan of something is an outline sketch.

clue.text: Rhyming intriguer

parts.note: a schemer or shrewd operator whose name for themselves is a two-part phrase whose halves rhyme

explanation.definitionFit: A sharp operator who makes deals by scheming is a schemer, and the two halves of the phrase rhyme.

clue.text: Went slowly in turning tree' into strange idol

indicators.note: one jumbled word is put inside the other, as the clue says one goes into the second
strange suggests the letters of idol are put into an odd order
turning suggests the letters of tree are churned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone dawdled while carving a tree into an odd idol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes TERE from TREE, and 'strange' makes LOID from IDOL; TERE goes into LOID.
explanation.definitionFit: To dawdle or linger is to move slowly with no purpose.

clue.text: The eye for a language with a letter missing

indicators.note: says one letter is dropped from the language named, here the leading C

parts.note: Coptic is the language of the Egyptian Christian church

explanation.surface: A dictionary remark that the eye's word is a language missing one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic is a humorous or literary noun for the eye, the organ of sight.

clue.text: Pudding has a turn after the 'sweet has been started

indicators.note: says the other pieces follow the opening letter
only the opening of the word sweet is taken, as if the sweet has just been begun

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: At dinner, someone gets a turn of pudding once dessert has begun.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a starchy milk pudding made from palm pith grains.

clue.text: Rung about when terrified about an article on it

clue.text: Most important when concerned with an area of the country

parts.note: over can mean about or concerning, as in a row over money
a Riding was one of the three old divisions of Yorkshire, a county in northern England

explanation.surface: A remark about which region of the nation matters most.
explanation.definitionFit: An overriding concern is one that takes priority above all others.

clue.text: Hanging for inaugurating deadly crime

indicators.note: the first letter of deadly opens the word, inaugurating it

parts.note: rape is a serious crime

explanation.surface: A death sentence of hanging handed down for the first of a series of deadly crimes.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtain or hanging cloth is a drape.

clue.text: In a flower goddess unprepared for death

parts.note: taken as written
a flower is something that flows, a river: the Test is a river in Hampshire, a county in southern England
Ate is the Greek goddess of folly and ruin

explanation.surface: A goddess among the flowers finds herself unready to die.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a crossword favourite for a river, a thing that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dies without having made a will is said to die in that state.

clue.text: Put up wrongly to vary, the sign

indicators.note: wrongly shows the letters are put in an incorrect order

explanation.surface: An instruction to put up a notice wrongly, changing the sign.
explanation.definitionFit: To be put up by a host is to be lodged until morning.

clue.text: Wave to the vessel, for It ALES gives one an exciting ride

parts.note: a roller is a big breaking wave
a coaster is a ship trading along the coast

explanation.surface: A big wave sweeps toward a ship, giving its passengers a thrilling ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It ALES' looks like a printing slip in the source; the parse needs only the two pieces and the ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground track with steep drops and sharp turns is a thrill ride.

clue.text: Where to see an important contribution to the innings?

definitions.meaning: a covered tier of seats at a sports ground, from which spectators watch

definitions.text: an important contribution to the innings?
definitions.meaning: read as a grand (big) stand, a long cricket partnership between two batsmen

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a stand is a partnership between two batsmen; a big one is a grand stand.
explanation.definitionFit: The main seating at a ground is the best place to watch, and a big batting partnership is a big stand.

clue.text: Noticed a sign in the grass on back

indicators.note: the sign sits within the grass, so 'in' places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet ground
a mark is a sign or symbol

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a sign lying in the grass behind them.
explanation.definitionFit: To remark something can mean to notice or observe it.

clue.text: Went over to the other side impleted on behalf of the departed, so it is said

definitions.text: Went over to the other side

indicators.note: signals that the words are heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: for means on behalf of; the dead are those who have departed this life

explanation.surface: Someone crossed over to the other side, speaking on behalf of the dead, like a medium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went over to the other side' suggests dying, but it means crossed a river by wading.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossing a river at a shallow point by wading is the past tense of the verb.

clue.text: Something which may grow out of loveless toll and union"

indicators.note: love is nil, the letter O, so loveless drops an O

parts.note: labour is toil
the NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, a British trade union

explanation.surface: Something growing out of loveless toil and a union, like a political movement.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis scoring love is zero, the letter O, so 'loveless' takes an O out.
explanation.definitionFit: A small tree with hanging yellow flowers is a growing thing.

clue.text: Shoot back and, obtain precinct some gold

indicators.note: back means the word for shoot is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to gun is to shoot
to get is to obtain

explanation.surface: A gunfight over a precinct ends with someone grabbing gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' reads as a noun, a young plant growth, but it is the verb; 'precinct' looks like a printing slip in the source.
explanation.definitionFit: A lump of native gold found in the ground is a small piece of it.

clue.text: Looks of gravity over weapons

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity
lances are long spears

explanation.surface: Grave looks cast over a stack of weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick looks are glances, brief views.

clue.text: Flower which gives the reverse of welcome to a sprinkling of rain

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell, the opposite of a greeting

indicators.note: a sprinkling scatters the letters of rain about

explanation.surface: A flower that bids farewell to a light shower.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a garden plant with pink or white flower heads, also used as a herbal remedy.

clue.text: Is one holding the king up as a mediterraneanperson?

indicators.note: the outer pieces hold the king's name within them

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the king's name reads from bottom to top

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: A question whether someone carrying a king aloft is from the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: The king here is Shakespeare's Lear; 'up' turns his name over in this down entry, and it sits between IS and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the state on the eastern Mediterranean shore is a national of it.

clue.text: Hot-looking athlete or climber

parts.note: scarlet is a fiery red colour
a runner is a track athlete

explanation.surface: A flushed athlete, or perhaps a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A bean plant with red flowers that twines up canes is a climbing plant.

clue.text: A craft discovered in extra deep water

indicators.note: the letters are found within the run of words extra deep water

explanation.surface: A boat found in very deep water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' suggests a boat, but it means a skilled occupation.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled occupation such as carpentry is a craft or calling.

clue.text: Comfortable since weapons have gone up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word for weapons reads from bottom to top

parts.note: guns are weapons

explanation.surface: Feeling at ease now the guns have been raised.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosy and warm is comfortable.

clue.text: Place for putting colour

definitions.meaning: the closely mown area around a golf hole where players putt
the hue of grass and leaves

explanation.definitionFit: The golf term for the putting surface shares its name with a hue of grass.

clue.text: In case it is cold, I should like something to eat

indicators.note: the answer sits in the run of letters across cold, I should, so 'In' signals a hidden run

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a bite to eat in case the weather turns cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In case' reads as 'just in case', but 'In' alone points inside the words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A prepared plate of food served at a meal is something to eat.

clue.text: Making allowances, I go after a soldier in love-making

indicators.note: the soldier and I go inside the word for love-making

parts.note: petting is kissing and caressing

indicators.note: the I follows the soldier

parts.note: RM is a Royal Marine

explanation.surface: Being tolerant while a soldier interrupts some love-making.
explanation.definitionFit: Allowing or letting something happen is making allowance for it.
